findings.title: Freeze receipt does not bind the full policy/opponent execution boundary
findings.evidence: Frozen sourceHashes bind nine first-party sources but omit src/chess.mjs and the resolved chess.js dependency/lock. Sparse legal action enumeration and position encoding depend on that unbound import. Python chess/torch/numpy execution versions are also absent from this freeze. The paired Stockfish executable is hashed after each game, but its digest is never required to equal a pre-exposure frozen expected digest (a prior generator engine digest exists in data-protocol.json). Therefore changed legal-move code/dependencies or an opponent replacement can pass all current frozen-source assertions. Artifact hashes do verify the eight candidate files, but do not close this execution provenance gap.
findings.impact: The implementation supports a narrower claim: listed sources and candidate bytes are frozen. It cannot alone certify the requested all-source/artifact freeze for heldout/pair evidence. No claim is made that files actually changed or results are wrong.
findings.requestedChange: Do not edit the frozen selector/evaluator or receipts during the active run. Resolve the current claim using genuinely pre-exposure immutable dependency/engine evidence if available; otherwise explicitly qualify the current run and retain controls pending an authorized fully bound run. For a future protocol, freeze/check src/chess.mjs, dependency lock/resolved chess.js bytes and Python runtime package identities, plus the paired opponent binary digest, before exposure and at completion. Add negative tests for an unbound dependency/opponent change. Do not retrofit newly computed hashes as proof of pre-exposure freezing.
